table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Delay - 1st Cylinder
table.description: How decel fuel cut works here: after the throttle closes, a timer starts; fuel is cut in one cylinder after D1, in a second cylinder D2 later, and in all cylinders D3 after that (the cut is staged so the car does not jerk). This table is D1: how long fuel keeps flowing after you lift off, by gear and engine speed. Bigger value = later cut (softer, more fuel into a hot exhaust: more pops on overrun); smaller = earlier cut (more engine braking). This is the normal table; the '(Alt)' copy replaces it under a condition that is not identified. Confirmed in code: address, layout, gear/RPM selection. Not confirmed: the time unit (8 ms per step: the same tick as the time-since-start counter, which logs confirm at 8 ms, but this timer itself is not measured yet), which of Normal/Alt is used while driving - check with a log.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Delay - 1st Cylinder (Alt)
table.description: Alternative copy of 'Decel Fuel Cut Delay - 1st Cylinder' (D1, by gear and engine speed). The ECU switches to it when RAM 0xFFFF6168 is not 0; what that flag means is not known yet. If you change the delays, change both tables the same way until a log shows which one is active.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Delay - 1st Cylinder (Special)
table.description: D1 (delay before the first cylinder is cut) used instead of the per-gear tables in a special mode, by engine speed only. The mode is active when function 0x22BAE returns 0 and more than 'Decel Fuel Cut Special Condition Threshold' (0.3 s) has passed since engine start - so in practice it is decided by 0x22BAE alone. What the mode is in real driving is not identified; it is not neutral (neutral uses 'Decel Fuel Cut Delay (Neutral)').

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Delay - 1st Cylinder (Special)(Alt)
table.description: Alternative copy of 'Decel Fuel Cut Delay - 1st Cylinder (Special)', used when RAM 0xFFFF6168 is not 0 (flag meaning not known).

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Delay - 2nd Cylinder / All Cylinders
table.description: How decel fuel cut works here: after the throttle closes, a timer starts; fuel is cut in one cylinder after D1, in a second cylinder D2 later, and in all cylinders D3 after that (the cut is staged so the car does not jerk). This table holds D2 ('2nd cyl' columns: from the first cut cylinder to the second) and D3 ('all' columns: from the second until fuel is cut in all cylinders), per gear plus the 'Special' mode, by engine speed. Total time until full cut = D1 + D2 + D3. Confirmed in code: address, layout, the 1 -> 2 -> all staging. Not confirmed: the time unit (8 ms per step: the same tick as the time-since-start counter, which logs confirm at 8 ms, but this timer itself is not measured yet).

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Delay - 2nd Cylinder / All Cylinders (Alt)
table.description: Alternative copy of 'Decel Fuel Cut Delay - 2nd Cylinder / All Cylinders' (D2 and D3), used when RAM 0xFFFF6168 is not 0 (flag meaning not known).

table.name: Overrun Fueling Cut Counter RPM Threshold
table.description: Engine speed boundaries that split the decel fuel cut delay tables into ranges: below 1st value, between 1st and 2nd, between 2nd and 3rd, above 3rd. These are the 'Engine Speed' ranges in the 'Decel Fuel Cut Delay' tables, so if you move a boundary, the meaning of those rows/columns moves with it. Confirmed: in code and in SubaruDefs (same table on AZ1G101N, address 0xC7B94 there).

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Delay (Neutral)
table.description: Delay used in neutral instead of all the per-gear tables: fuel is cut in all cylinders at once after this time (no staging), at any engine speed. Neutral comes from RAM 0xFFFF67CB = 1, the gearbox neutral switch (confirmed by the owner and by logs: 1 at idle in neutral, short pulses while shifting). Stock value is about 0.1 s, so on a blip in neutral fuel is cut almost at once and comes back at the resume threshold (about 2000 RPM at a standstill, see 'Overrun Fueling RPM Resume Threshold'); this lean cut-and-resume is the likely cause of pops when revving in neutral. A bigger value keeps fuel on during short blips (fewer pops, slower RPM drop).

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Special Condition Threshold
Threshold
table.data: Time since engine start at least

table.description: Threshold for the 'Special' delay mode: the mode needs RAM 0xFFFF5F8C to be at least this value. 0xFFFF5F8C is the time since engine start: 8 ms per count, stops at 65535 (about 524 s); confirmed by logs. Stock 38 counts = 0.3 s, so this condition is met almost always and the mode is really decided by the other check (function 0x22BAE, not identified). Leave as is.

table.name: Overrun Fueling RPM Resume Threshold
table.description: Engine speed at which fuel cut is allowed and below which the injectors switch back on when coasting with the throttle closed, by coolant temperature (cold engine - higher, warm - 900 RPM). Raise it if the engine stumbles or stalls when fuel comes back; lower it for longer fuel cut. The code adds to it: +1100 RPM when vehicle speed is below 17 (unit not confirmed), plus hysteresis, so at a standstill, in neutral, fuel comes back at about 2000 RPM with a warm engine; logs agree with this. The offsets are not exposed as tables yet (floats 0xC7D30-0xC7D68). Confirmed: in code and in SubaruDefs (same table on AZ1G101N, address 0xCA2F0 there).

table.name: Overrun Enrich RPM Delta Activation
table.description: Taken from SubaruDefs for AZ1G101N (0xC7B40 there; the address is moved by the same +0x1D8 as the other overrun tables and the value matches). SubaruDefs: the RPM change needed to turn on the extra fuel when fueling resumes after overrun. Not checked in code. Leave as is.

table.name: Overrun initial injector enrichment (pulsewidth)
table.description: Taken from SubaruDefs for AZ1G101N (0xC7B44 there; the address is moved by the same +0x1D8 as the other overrun tables and the value matches). SubaruDefs: the extra injector pulse added at the moment fueling resumes after overrun, so the engine picks up smoothly. Not checked in code. Leave as is.
